content.title: Labeled snapshots, not an SLA
content.lede: The current generic CLI is faster than wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6.1 at every tested report size. The public Go library path is about 20x faster than the wkhtmltopdf CLI at 2 pages. Peak RSS is lower through 50 pages and higher from 100 pages. The 2026-09-11 perf-improve capture met the 240 MB 500-page B/op acceptance and cut warm 500-page allocation by 26.9% and warm matrix time by 17.5% against the pre-improve capture; the 1.10 s warm-time acceptance is still open. Open the Benchmarks page for the visual comparison.

content.title: B/op acceptance met, 1.10 s warm-time acceptance open
content.body: The 2026-09-11 perf-improve capture put warm 500-page B/op at 234.92 MB (warm matrix) and 235.50 MB (standalone median), at or below the 240 MB acceptance and slightly below the 0.2.4 237.76 MB row. The public library median is 236.91 MB, at parity with its 236.85 MB row (0.03% above). Warm 500-page time is 1,228.72 ms (warm matrix) and 1,297.98 ms (standalone median): about 17.5% better than the pre-improve 1,489.42 ms matrix row, but still above the 1.010 s Snapshot I row and the 1.10 s acceptance. The fastest 500-page row in the capture is 1,186.48 ms. Raw evidence: plans/0.2.6/perf-improve/results/phase-7/final-capture.md.

content.title: Generic CLI, not the island-era path
content.body: The 2026-09-11 CLI comparison rows are the generic convert path against wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6.1 with patched Qt, from the dated recovery capture; the phase-7 capture measured gowkhtmltopdf only in cli-rss mode. The current in-process and library engine rows are three independent 1x samples per workload from the perf-improve capture, one fresh process each; the reported value is the median of the three raw samples and B/op is never averaged. 2-page B/op includes the one-time default-font work (about 2.7 MB on the internal path), so it is not like-for-like with the 2026-08-19 multi-iteration matrix. Median of three timed process runs after one warmup for the CLI cells. Peak RSS is /usr/bin/time %M. Do not compare these RSS numbers to older island-era CLI snapshots, and do not treat Go B/op as process RSS.

content.heading: Historical public library PDF vs wkhtmltopdf CLI (2026-08-19, indicative)
Historical in-process PDF vs wkhtmltopdf CLI (2026-08-19, indicative)
What the numbers mean
items: CLI comparison is process wall time plus peak RSS for freshly built gowkhtmltopdf versus the installed wkhtmltopdf binary.

The current CLI comparison matrix comes from the dated 2026-09-11 recovery capture on the uncommitted 0.2.6 working tree (VERSION 0.2.5); the engine rows come from the 2026-09-11 perf-improve phase-7 capture on the same tree, which measured gowkhtmltopdf only. The in-process and library rows are three independent 1x samples per workload; the published value is the median of the three raw values and B/op is never averaged.

2-page B/op rows include the one-time default-font work (about 2.7 MB on the internal path) because each sample is a fresh 1x process. Do not compare them to the 2026-08-19 multi-iteration matrix without that caveat.

The public Go library rows call Document.WritePDF and ImageDocument.WriteImage directly. The approximately 20x landing claim keeps the dated recovery-capture boundary: 258 ms divided by 10.88 ms at 2 pages, using the wkhtmltopdf CLI as the baseline.
WeasyPrint and Puppeteer use the same generated report fixture; Puppeteer RSS includes the Node driver and headless Chrome process tree.
The report fixture is testdata/golden/benchmarks/templates/report.html.tmpl with 20 invoice rows per requested page.
Page islands (convert.NewBenchmarkPDFRequest) are a benchmark-only opt-in. Ordinary CLI and library requests stay on the generic path.
Full matrices, historical snapshots, and raw go test rows live in testdata/golden/benchmarks/, documentation/performance.md, and plans/0.2.6/perf-improve/results/phase-7/.
